speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the nature of your chest pain and when your vomiting began. To understand the severity, have you experienced any shortness of breath or sweating? REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG).

speaker: Doctor
text: With a normal ECG, let's narrow this down. Have you noticed any abdominal pain, fever, or changes in your stool like clay-colored color? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests; REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: Good news, your liver function tests and abdominal ultrasound are normal. Since your chest pain and vomiting persist despite a normal ECG, have you noticed any pain radiating to your back, jaw, or left arm? Also, do you have a history of gallstones or recent heavy meals?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture). The combination of forceful vomiting after alcohol consumption, followed by sudden chest pain and choking, is highly suggestive of an esophageal tear. This is a medical emergency requiring immediate surgical consultation.
